d1.for_report: D1 distilled five classical planning doctrines into machine-readable, fully sourced recipes (V06/doctrine_recipes.json, sources annotated in doctrine_sources.md). Every number carries provenance, a confidence grade, and a doctrine_silent flag: 43 graded quantities in total (29 high, 13 medium, 1 low confidence) and 30 explicitly marked silences. Verified anchors include Howard's 6,000-acre estate / 1,000-acre town / 32,000 people with 26% of town land in stated green (Central Park 145 + Grand Avenue 115 acres); Corbusier's 1,000 persons/ha housing sector at 5-12% ground coverage under 12-60-storey buildings; Perry's 160-acre, 5,000-6,000-person unit with 10% open space and a 400-m school radius; the SNiP microrayon's 8,000-12,000 people on 10-60 ha with >=6 m2/person green and a 500-m service limit inside an uncrossable superblock; and GB 50180-2018's nested life circles (100k/25k/12k persons) decomposed into 2-4 ha blocks governed by coupled FAR (1.0-3.1), coverage (22-43%), green-rate (25-35%) and height (18-80 m) caps on a dense 150-250 m road grid. Where sources conflicted (Ville Radieuse coverage; GB green-per-capita extraction), ranges or documented discards were recorded instead of invented precision. The stakeholder a-priori vectors render who each text empowers: Howard's cooperative trust (resident_community .90), Corbusier's technocratic Authority (government .95), Perry's double-faced unit (resident .70 AND developer .60 — community ideal sold as a subdivision template), the microrayon's state monopoly (government .95, developer .00), and GB50180's norm-setting state times executing developer (.80/.70). Each carries an anachronism note where the China-derived four-dimension vocabulary strains. Caoyang New Village (1951, planner Wang Dingzeng) was verified as the PRC's first workers' new village planned on Perry's principles (school-centred, ~600 m radius, >=10% open space) and is attached to both neighbourhood_unit and microrayon as the study's empirical hinge: a community doctrine executed by a state client, sitting physically inside our Shanghai token vocabulary. A systematic negative result matters for the next tasks: doctrines are most silent precisely where generation is hungriest (residential and road land fractions, coverage for the pre-war doctrines), so the generator must declare its fill-in policy rather than pretend doctrinal completeness. The comparative chart is at fig/fig_d1_doctrines.png; summary statistics in results_d1.json.
honest_notes: GB50180 per-capita residential-area land for 15-min circles (22-28 m2/person) rests on a single full-text extraction of Table 4.0.1 and is flagged low confidence — re-verify before any quantitative use.

Microrayon kindergarten 300 m / school 750 m radii are standard SNiP 2.07.01-89 table values widely cited in secondary literature but were NOT re-verified against the table text itself today; kept at medium confidence.
Ville Radieuse housing-sector 12% ground coverage is the canonical La Ville radieuse quote, but today's web sources only confirmed a 5-15% towers-in-park band; recorded as range [0.05, 0.12], medium.

The five stakeholder configs are ASSERTED doctrine-level priors (who the text empowers), not observations; the additive 4-dim format flattens hybrid sequencing — GB50180 is a state pen moving a developer hand, and a static vector cannot express that order.

Land-budget denominators differ across doctrines (town / sector / unit / microdistrict / block); any cross-doctrine comparison or 1-km generation must normalize explicitly — left to the generation task by design.

Systematic finding, not a bug: every doctrine is most silent exactly where the generator is hungriest (residential fraction, road land, coverage for the older three) — classical doctrines fix the symbolic core (green, school, density) and leave the economic residual unwritten; silence counts run 4-7 fields per doctrine.

Counting method: confidence counts (29 high / 13 medium / 1 low) tally quantity-level 'confidence' fields in the recipes JSON via the script, excluding the stakeholder configs which carry their own separate confidences (3 high / 2 medium).

d2.for_report: D2 translated the five D1 doctrine recipes into the measured Shanghai 50-m token vocabulary, producing per-paradigm 400-cell token budgets, demanded semantic mixes, five 20x20 typed-void skeletons (skeleton_*.npy with E_ROAD/E_GREEN/E_VACANT and RESERVED-CIVIC cells), a transparent claim-by-claim translation table (translation.json), and an 18-entry expressiveness audit. Every allocation cites its doctrine quantity and every geometric constant (ring radii, band widths, grid spacings) carries its source. Density anchors land close: Ville Radieuse 1,021 p/ha vs the doctrinal 1,000 (solved from Corbusier's own 14 m2/person cell against measured T6 GFA, with block coverage .094 falling inside the doctrinal 5-12%); microrayon 330 p/ha by construction; Perry 94 vs 77-93; Howard 62 vs 74 (road/industry quantization eats lots, reported as deviation). GB 50180 is the cleanest translation: a T4/T6 split solved for block FAR 2.50 simultaneously satisfies all three coupled caps (coverage .17<=.22, green .325>=.30) — unsurprising, since the standard was written for this fabric. The audit is the headline result. The vocabulary cannot say: very-tall-AND-nearly-no-footprint (Corbusier's 200-m cruciforms at 5% coverage — T8 is half the height with coverage .99, inverting the open ground; the known no-true-high-rise data ceiling); slab-at-50-m (T3 is slab at 22 m, T6 is tower at 60 m — VR's a-redent becomes point towers); anything below T1's 10-m height (Howard's and Perry's 1-2-storey cottages inflate ~1.5-2x); 6-fold radial geometry; grade-separated motorways. Carrying 1,000 p/ha with 60-m Shanghai towers forces a tower every 100 m where the doctrine wants one colossus per 400-m module: many short towers where the text says few tall ones. Two reversals are notable: the measured Shanghai high-rise token T6 violates GB 50180's own cell-level caps (cov .31 vs .22, h 60.4 vs 54 m), with compliance re-emerging only through green embedding at block level; and the microrayon translation, density-anchored, honestly leaves 31% of ground as unprogrammed E_VACANT — a faithful rendering of SNiP's land-balance silence. Civic cells are carried by T2, chosen because pools give T2 the highest measured public_admin share. The skeletons and budgets are ready for semantic-conditioned generation (D3); designated commercial/industrial cell coordinates are exported per paradigm.
honest_notes: 50-m cell quantization systematically overstates road land: GB 50180 grid takes 36% of cells (vs ~15-20% real) even though its 8 km/km2 network-density norm is hit exactly; Garden City roads take 24% where Howard is acreage-silent. Downstream indicator comparisons must use the block-land denominators recorded in translation.json, not raw cell fractions.

Garden City window FAR (1.48) is inflated by the 44 T7 cells standing in for ~10-m factory sheds and the glass arcade (T7 is 29.4 m, GFA 30k m2/cell); its residential fraction lands at .27 vs the doctrinal .33 and implied density 62 vs 74 p/ha. Deviations are reported, not hidden.

Five per-capita floorspace assumptions (22/14/40/15/35 m2 GFA/person) are translation-layer numbers BEYOND the D1 recipes; each is labeled with its rationale in translation.json (PERSONS dict). Only Corbusier's 14 m2 is a doctrine-internal number; the others are indicative.

VR business district is omitted from the window (the D1 land-budget denominator is the housing sector) — so VR's semantic mix is 100% residential_estate and office_finance never appears in any paradigm. The doctrine-claims-vs-fabric comparison in later phases should remember the omission is by construction.
Perry's principle 4 (all dwellings within 400 m of the school) fails at window corners because the 800-m unit was stretched to the 1,000-m window (+25%); recorded as a gap, not patched.

T7 (118 buildings) and T8 (29) pools are thin; semantic-conditioned draws for T7-commercial (~24% of pool) leave ~28 candidate buildings — generation may show repetition along the GB podium row and Garden City arcade.
Skeleton -1 (RESERVED-CIVIC) cells are counted inside the T2 budget entries; consumers must read reserved_civic_semantics for their demanded semantics rather than treating all T2 as residential.
Initial run had a real bug (implied density used total GFA including industry/podium, giving Garden City 674 p/ha); fixed to residential-GFA-only before final outputs.

d3.for_report: D3 generated all ten canvases (five 1 km units, five 3 km composites) from the D2 budgets and skeletons, seed 0, and rendered the owner's money shot: fig_d3_gallery.png shows the five doctrines side by side as figure-ground plans over their typed-void skeletons with height-coloured axonometrics below. The fabrics are immediately distinguishable — Howard's concentric cottage bands inside a rail ring, Corbusier's tower lattice in continuous green, Perry's fine single-family grain with corner shops, the microrayon's slab rows on a green spine, and GB 50180's tower-north/slab-south superblocks. Placement is prescriptive-first: each doctrine's own geometry (industry ring alternating shed/yard, Crystal Palace arcade by angle, corner-graded apartment cells, sun-spacing tower/slab rows) deterministically places the D2 token budget, and the learned Shanghai adjacency is used only where a doctrine is genuinely silent — which turned out to be only the microrayon's free-plan cells (170 of 228), arranged by 3 multiset-preserving Metropolis sweeps labelled 'Shanghai accent'. All five units match their D2 budgets exactly. The semantic-conditioned collage (v05's named next step) preferred pool cells whose GFA-dominant building semantic matches each cell's demanded semantic: the fallback rate was 0.0 on all ten canvases, but this hides near-singleton supply — T2-education exists as only 2 cells in the entire measured pool, so every school in every paradigm is one of two real Shanghai cells, and Howard's 32 industry cells draw from 3 industrial pool cells; reuse counts are reported per semantic. Achieved indicators: unit FAR 1.28/1.18/0.46/0.65/1.97 against D2 targets 1.48/1.43/0.40/0.63/1.99 — GB 50180 and the microrayon land within 0.04 (the standard was written for this fabric), while Howard and Corbusier undershoot by ~0.2 because their budgets were solved on token-mean GFA and the pools draw below it. Composites follow documented assembly rules: Social-City core + 6 satellites in an agricultural belt (360 cells lost to compressed spacing, counted), 3x3 Radiant City with a T8 office head-of-axis unit that visibly inverts Corbusier's open ground into a coverage-.99 mat (the audit failure, shown not hidden), 2x2 Perry units with a T7 town centre at the shared junction, 2x2 microrayons on a 100 m transit corridor, and 2x2 superblocks flanking a 200 m fifteen-minute civic strip. Everything D4 needs — per-building semantic, demanded semantic, match flag, token, source window — is in cache_gen/{unit,city}_<paradigm>.parquet.
honest_notes: Collage realization undershoots the D2 budget expectation where the budget was solved against token-mean GFA: garden_city unit FAR 1.28 vs 1.48, ville_radieuse 1.18 vs 1.43 (pool draws land below the token mean); microrayon and gb50180 land within 0.02-0.04. The token composition is exact — the gap is pool-draw variance, not placement.

Zero semantic fallbacks across all 10 canvases is NOT pool abundance: the pool serves every demand but sometimes from near-singleton stock. T2-education has only 2 cells in all of Shanghai's TRAIN pool (every doctrinal school in every paradigm is a copy of one of 2 real cells); T7-industrial has 3 cells serving Howard's 32 industry-ring cells. Unique-pool-cells-used counts are in results_d3.json per semantic.

The Ville Radieuse business centre is the audit failure made visible: T8 = 94 m, coverage .99 megastructure standing in for 200 m, 5%-coverage cruciforms — the open ground is inverted into a solid mat (see city figure, top centre). Known no-true-high-rise data ceiling.
Howard's and Perry's 1-2-storey cottages cannot exist in the vocabulary (T1 floor is 10 m): unit h_p90 21 m / 13 m instead of ~8 m.

Garden-city composite: 7 towns at true Howard spacing do not fit 3 km; satellites overlap (360 cells lost, centre-first precedence) so the composite reads as one continuous 7-ward city rather than separated towns with rail between — a quantization deviation, documented in the assembly rule.

Only the microrayon actually invoked the Shanghai-accent Gibbs (170 cells); the other four doctrines fully prescribe their micro-arrangement. The Shanghai accent still enters everywhere through the collage itself — every building is a real Shanghai building.
Composite city FARs are diluted by doctrine periphery (green belt / unspecified context) in the 9 km2 denominator; compare unit indicators for fabric intensity.
Composite axons were skipped (plan-only city figures) for runtime; the task marked them optional.

d4.for_report: D4 ran the v05 power-attribution chain verbatim over all ten generated canvases (five 1-km doctrine units, five 3x3-km composites): building semantic -> literature prior cell -> GFA-weighted 4-dim profile, unlabeled excluded (max 3% of GFA). Because generated buildings carry no construction year, every residential_estate falls into the low-confidence no_age cell (gov .4 / dev .5) — the documented v05 weakness, here kept deliberately: Chinese no-age priors reading Howard, Corbusier and the microrayon. The headline verifies: four of five doctrines flip their first-ranked stakeholder, and all four flips land on developer_capital. Garden City claims community .90, reads back dev .489; Ville Radieuse claims state .95, reads dev .499; microrayon claims state .95, reads dev .514; GB50180 claims state .80, reads dev .527. Only Perry's neighbourhood unit holds (res .70 claimed, res .513 read). L1 gaps run 0.71 (GB50180) to 1.28 (microrayon) and are scale-stable (unit vs 3-km composite differ by under 0.08). An exact per-dim decomposition via two counterfactual read-backs (swap donor semantics for the demanded program; swap no_age for the historically apt pre1985 danwei cell) splits each gap into (a) the no-age artifact, (b) collage semantic drift, (c) genuine program translation. The flips have two distinct anatomies. For the estate-heavy doctrines (Ville Radieuse, microrayon, GB50180; estates .70-.99 of GFA) the artifact dominates or co-dominates (L1 0.85/0.65/0.60) — a structural finding about the priors, not the fabric. But Garden City's flip carries zero artifact: its cottages avoided the estate cell entirely, and instead GFA-weighting hands the town to its own factory belt (.53 of GFA) and shopping arcade (.35), which the priors read as state-capital. Howard's cooperative ownership is invisible in form; what survives translation is the program's square meters. Even the most charitable counterfactual cannot reach a gov-.95 claim — the prior vocabulary saturates at .8 — so part of component (c) is vocabulary compression, disclosed. Collage drift (b) is negligible everywhere except the neighbourhood unit (0.22), whose held ranking anyway rests on the medium-low-confidence urban-village analogy covering 91% of its GFA. Outputs: results_d4.json, fig_d4_gap.png (dumbbells + L1 bars), fig_d4_decomp.png (signed stacked decomposition).
honest_notes: The headline holds but for two different reasons, and conflating them would be wrong: for ville_radieuse / microrayon / gb50180 the flip to developer_capital is substantially the no-age estate artifact (component a = 0.85 / 0.65 / 0.60 of L1; estates are .70-.99 of GFA and every one falls into the dev-.5 no_age cell). For garden_city the artifact is exactly zero (Howard's cottages were translated as residential_lowrise, not estate) and the flip is 100% genuine translation: GFA-weighting lets the factory belt (.53 of GFA) and shopping arcade (.35) drown the count-dominant cottages, and the priors read industrial/commercial as gov-dev. Howard loses his town to capital through his own industrial program, not through the age bug.

Even under the most charitable counterfactual R2 (perfect semantic fidelity + pre1985 danwei reading), no doctrine reaches its claim: the prior vocabulary tops out at gov .8 (public_admin) and the pre1985 estate cell at gov .7, so a gov-.95 claim (ville_radieuse, microrayon) is unreachable by construction — vocabulary compression is part of component (c) and should be stated in the report.

The one held ranking (neighbourhood_unit, res-first both ways) rests on the LEAST trustworthy prior: 90.6% of its labeled GFA flows through the residential_lowrise cell, which is a medium-low-confidence urban-village ANALOGY applied to lilong-like lowrise. Its read-back also acquires informal .31 that Perry never intended. 'Perry survives translation' is true only modulo that analogy.

Component (b) (collage semantic drift) is near zero everywhere except neighbourhood_unit (L1 0.22, driven by 3% unlabeled GFA and within-donor-cell semantic heterogeneity; building-level semantic mismatch 2-21% even though D3 cell-level fallback was 0). The generation pipeline is essentially not the source of the gap.

L1 component magnitudes (a)+(b)+(c) can exceed the net L1 gap due to sign cancellation between components (visible for ville_radieuse: 1.50 stacked vs 1.20 net); per-dim signed sums are exact, the L1 stack is not — both shown in fig_d4_decomp.
Decomposition is single-path (order b-then-a); a Shapley average over orders was not computed. Components a and b interact only through estate-GFA shares, so order effects are small but nonzero.

Read-back profiles are means of literature priors, not measurements of power; 'the fabric reads as developer-ish' means 'a v05-prior-equipped observer of contemporary Shanghai would attribute it so' — asserted-vs-observed discipline applies to both sides of the gap.

choices.choice: Run the v05 E2 chain verbatim (semantic -> prior cell -> GFA-weighted mean over labeled buildings, unlabeled excluded) rather than redesigning aggregation for generated fabrics
choices.alternatives: count-weighted or footprint-weighted aggregation; re-including unlabeled at baseline prior
choices.reason: comparability with the 24 real-Shanghai window profiles in v05/results_e2.json is the point of the read-back; changing the chain would confound doctrine effects with method effects. GFA-weighting consequences (big boxes dominate) are reported as a finding, not hidden.

choices.choice: Map ALL generated residential_estate buildings to the no_age prior cell (gov .4 / dev .5 / res .3 / inf .05, confidence low)
choices.alternatives: impute construction years from doctrine epoch (e.g. ville_radieuse -> pre1985); sample donor building ages from token_pools
choices.reason: generated buildings genuinely have no construction year; imputing epoch-consistent ages would fabricate data and pre-bake the answer. The no-age fallback is the v05-documented weakness, deliberately retained ('Chinese no-age priors reading Howard') and then quantified as decomposition component (a) instead of being patched.

choices.choice: Sequential counterfactual decomposition R0 (actual) -> R1 (swap donor-inherited semantics for D2-demanded semantics) -> R2 (swap estate cell no_age -> pre1985), giving per-dim gap = (c: apriori-R2) + (a: R2-R1) + (b: R1-R0) exactly
choices.alternatives: Shapley-style averaging over both swap orders; regression-based attribution; only the no_age->pre1985 bound the task suggested
choices.reason: the telescoping identity makes the decomposition exact and auditable per dim; demanded_semantic exists on every building (D3 logged it), making R1 well-defined. Single path (b before a) is order-dependent and disclosed; pre1985 is the historically apt cell for the pre-market doctrines (danwei/public-housing logic), so (a) is a meaningful bound, not arbitrary.

choices.choice: Use the unit canvases (1 km canonical modules) as the primary gap/decomposition object, with 3x3 km composites shown as secondary markers and a second L1 bar
choices.alternatives: average unit+city; city-primary
choices.reason: stakeholder_apriori is asserted at the doctrine-unit level (D1); composites add skeleton/edge effects. Empirically it barely matters: unit and city L1 gaps differ by <= 0.08, which itself is a robustness result worth showing.

choices.choice: Report ranking flip as argmax(apriori) vs argmax(read-back) only
choices.alternatives: full rank correlation (Kendall tau) over 4 dims
choices.reason: with 4 dims, two of which (informal) are near-zero in most doctrines, tau is noise-dominated; the first-dim flip is the interpretable headline and the signed per-dim gaps carry the rest.

d5.for_report: D5 places the five generated paradigm units on the v03 real-Shanghai signature cloud. The projection basis was rebuilt from first principles: 19-dim signatures (9 token shares + 10 indicators) recomputed for all 24 real windows from the v03 cache with the verbatim v03 formulas, z-scored on TRAIN mu/sd, PCA fit on the 18 TRAIN windows with v03's sign convention. The correctness gate passed decisively — maximum deviation from the stored pca_xy is 4.9e-05, far under the 1e-3 tolerance — so paradigm placements are in the authentic published basis. Typed voids (road/water/green, 116-300 of 400 cells per unit) were folded back into T0 for comparability, a disclosed loss: the cloud cannot distinguish doctrine parkland from vacancy. Placements are legible as doctrine: Ville Radieuse projects beyond the cloud's hull near Lujiazui CBD (PC2 6.6 vs real max 4.9) — towers-in-park exceeds anything real Shanghai builds at 1 km scale. GB50180 lands among CBD/office windows despite being a residential code. Garden City and Neighbourhood Unit land in the low-rise corner nearest peri-urban villages (A32/A33) and waterfront redevelopment (A47), though garden_city's 19-dim z-norm of 14.9 shows it is far off-manifold even where the 2-D view looks plausible — both PC-space and full z-space distances are reported throughout. The Caoyang anchor test is an honest miss: A13 ranks 14/24 (PC) and 11/24 (z) as neighbour of the generated neighbourhood_unit. The reason is legible in A13's own composition: Perry's distilled recipe encodes 1929 low-rise fabric (61% T1 houses, FAR 0.46, h_p90 13 m), but Caoyang today is slab/midrise (30% T3 + 20% T4, sh_slab .46, FAR 1.57, h_p90 37 m) — the 1951 adaptation built multi-storey workers' slabs and seven decades of rebuilding densified further. Strikingly, the generated microrayon near-passes instead (rank 9/24 PC, 6/24 z), and its family-share profile nearly matches A13 (slab .49 vs .46, mid .26 vs .27); the residual gap is pure density (FAR 0.65 vs 1.57). Interpretively (not asserted identity), built Caoyang reads closer to a densified Soviet microrayon than to Perry's American diagram — the miss localizes what the 1951 translation changed rather than indicting the pipeline, whose projection machinery passed its gate. Outputs: exp_cloud.py, results_d5.json, fig/fig_d5_cloud.png (visually verified, no label overlaps).
honest_notes: THE ANCHOR TEST IS A MISS, and an informative one: A13 Caoyang ranks only 14/24 (PC) and 11/24 (z) as neighbour of the generated neighbourhood_unit. The Perry recipe distilled in D2 encodes 1929 low-rise fabric (61% T1, sh_house .87, FAR 0.46), so it lands among peri-urban villages (A32/A33). A13 today is slab/midrise (30% T3 + 20% T4, sh_slab .46, FAR 1.57): the 1951 adaptation built multi-storey workers' slabs and 70 years of rebuilding densified further. Validation of the chain must therefore rest on the other paradigms' placements, not the anchor.

Near-miss consolation: the generated microrayon's family-share profile nearly matches A13 (slab .49 vs .46, mid .26 vs .27, median_fp 230 vs 262 m2); residual gap is density (FAR 0.65 vs 1.57) and void share (.72 vs .30). Interpretive reading only, not asserted identity: built Caoyang reads closer to a densified microrayon than to Perry's diagram.

Garden_city is severely off-manifold in full z-space (z-norm 14.9; nearest z-distance 12.8) despite sitting visually inside the cloud in PC view — driven by extreme tok_T1/tok_T7 shares relative to TRAIN sd. PC-space proximity overstates realism for off-manifold fabrics; both metrics are in results_d5.json.

Ville Radieuse projects beyond the real cloud's hull (PC2 = 6.6 vs real max 4.9, nearest = Lujiazui CBD): no real Shanghai residential window combines 87 m h_p90 with 7% coverage. GB50180, nominally a residential code, lands among CBD/office windows (A01/A04/A02) — useful for the stakeholder-gap reading downstream.

Void folding (116-300 of 400 cells per unit) erases the road/water/green typing the generator worked to produce; the cloud cannot reward doctrine parkland over vacancy. A 12-token cloud would need a refit basis and would break comparability with v03.

Reference set is only 24 windows (18 TRAIN), so ranks are coarse and the PCA basis is fit on n=18 with p=19 features; distances are meaningful but the cloud is a sketch of Shanghai's manifold, not a census.
Figure label placement needed three manual-offset passes (verified by zoomed crops); final render has no overlaps.

choices.choice: Recomputed the 19-dim signature matrix for all 24 real windows from the v03 cache (cells.parquet token grids + library.parquet buildings) using the verbatim formulas in run_v03.py::signatures(), instead of reusing the 4-decimal-rounded values stored in signatures.json.
choices.alternatives: Rebuild M from the rounded token_comp/indicators stored in signatures.json.
choices.reason: Makes the correctness gate meaningful: reproduction error is 4.9e-05 (pure float/rounding of stored pca_xy), so any paradigm projection error would be attributable to my code, not input rounding.

choices.choice: Replicated v03's exact projection arithmetic: TRAIN-only mu/sd (ddof=0), PCA(2, random_state=0) fit on 18 TRAIN z-rows, XY = Z @ comps.T with no mean re-centering, then sign-flip so each PC's top-|loading| feature is positive.
choices.alternatives: Use sklearn pca.transform() (subtracts pca.mean_) or refit PCA on all 24 windows.
choices.reason: The stored pca_xy were produced by exactly this code path; only verbatim replication passes the 1e-3 gate and guarantees paradigms are projected in the same basis as the published cloud.

choices.choice: Folded typed voids 9/10/11 (road/water/green) back into T0 before computing paradigm token shares, with per-unit folded counts disclosed in results_d5.json.
choices.alternatives: Extend the cloud to 12 tokens (breaks reproduction of the stored basis) or drop void cells (distorts shares).
choices.reason: The v03 cloud knows only one undifferentiated void; folding is the only comparable mapping. Disclosure matters because the cloud then cannot distinguish doctrine parkland from vacancy — e.g. Ville Radieuse's 224 green cells read as generic void.

choices.choice: Reported nearest neighbours and anchor ranks in BOTH 2-dim PC space and full 19-dim z-space, plus each paradigm's z-norm.
choices.alternatives: PC-space only (what the figure shows).
choices.reason: PC1+PC2 capture only 56.8% of variance; garden_city has PC-distance 0.80 to A47 but z-distance 12.79 (z-norm 14.88) — PC proximity alone would falsely suggest the fabric is Shanghai-like when it is far off-manifold.

choices.choice: Used paradigm UNITS (1 km, 20x20) only; ranked A13 among all 24 real windows (TRAIN + HELDOUT) for the anchor test.
choices.alternatives: Project 3-km composites too; rank among TRAIN only.
choices.reason: Units match the real windows' 1 km support (composites are not cloud-comparable, per task); A13 is itself a TRAIN window so including HELDOUT in the ranking adds competitors without leakage.

choices.choice: Indicators recomputed from unit_*.parquet with v03 formulas and cross-checked against results_d3.json (2% tolerance, no warnings fired) rather than copied from D3.
choices.alternatives: Trust D3's indicator block directly.
choices.reason: D3 names/rounding differ slightly (height_p50 vs h_p50, median_fp_area); recomputing guarantees the exact estimator (np.percentile, fp-weighted family shares) matches the cloud's.

d6.for_report: D6 inverts the pipeline: instead of asking what a doctrine's fabric reads as, we ask which doctrine (or 50/50 blend) to prescribe for a target stakeholder. Fifteen candidates — the five D2 doctrine budgets plus all ten pairwise blends (budgets averaged, largest-remainder to 400 cells; skeleton and civic program from the first-named parent; per-token semantics = mean of the parents' measured per-token distributions) — were ranked against three v05-E4 targets (GOV-, DEV-, RES-first) on a deterministic expectation: per built token, count x expected labeled GFA per pool cell x the token pool's GFA-weighted mean v05 prior vector (estates on the no-age cell), normalized. Winners by L1 (cosine reported): GOV-first selects the neighbourhood_unit+microrayon blend (expected L1 0.754, realized 0.827); DEV-first selects pure Ville Radieuse (0.347, realized 0.550); RES-first selects pure Neighbourhood Unit (1.046, realized 0.488). For GOV-first the two metrics disagreed and the expected-L1 margin over pure NU was 0.0021 — inside surrogate error — so we generated both: the realized fabrics favor the blend (0.827 vs 1.128). Three findings matter. First, GOV-first is unreachable: expected government spans only .37-.41 across all fifteen candidates, because civic GFA is budget-capped and ageless estates read gov .4; the gov-heavy danwei reading lives in building AGE, which no token budget can express — morphology alone cannot make a fabric read government-first, echoing D4 from the inverse direction. Second, the expectation surrogate fails exactly where semantic conditioning works: pool-average power dilutes residential_lowrise priors with the T1/T2 pools' mixed donors, so NU's realized profile lands 0.674 L1 away from its expectation — and closer to the target. Third, the irony: the best fabric for a developer-capital target is Le Corbusier's, the doctrine claiming gov .95. Every number is single-seed (seed 0) and the entire search optimizes ASSERTED profiles built from literature priors — it selects doctrines under our priors' worldview, nothing more; this caveat is stamped on the figure (fig_d6_invert.png: three columns of plan, axon, and target/expected/realized bars). Full 15x3 ranking, winner gaps, reconciliation counts, and the post-hoc disagreement check are in results_d6.json.
honest_notes: The whole search optimizes ASSERTED profiles assembled from literature priors (TF/v05/power_priors_v05.json). It selects doctrines under our priors' worldview, nothing more; it does not predict who would hold power in a built fabric. Stated in _meta, figure footnote, and ILLUSTRATIVE NOT PREDICTIVE stamp.

GOV-first is unreachable by any candidate: expected government spans only .372-.410 across all 15 candidates (target .8). Doctrine budgets cap civic GFA at a few percent and no-age estates read gov .4; the gov-heavy danwei reading (gov .7) lives in the pre-1985 AGE cell, which generated buildings cannot carry. As in D4, the missing variable is time/tenure, not form: no token budget can morph a fabric into reading government-first under no-age priors.

The expectation surrogate is poor exactly where semantic conditioning bites: T1/T2 pools are semantically heterogeneous, so pool-average power dilutes residential_lowrise (res .6 / inf .4) with commercial/estate donors; neighbourhood_unit's expected-vs-realized L1 is 0.674 while semantically homogeneous candidates are well predicted (microrayon 0.094, garden_city 0.122 in the pure sanity check). The surrogate is systematically biased toward the pool's developer-leaning mean, which means RES-first-style rankings could in principle be wrong; pure NU is also the realized-best among D4's five pures for resident weight (R0 res .513), so the RES pick survives the realized check.

GOV-first winner margin was 0.0021 expected L1 (NU+MR over pure NU) — far inside surrogate error; cosine disagreed. Disclosed, picked by L1 per spec, and the added single-seed realized cross-check happened to favor the blend decisively (0.827 vs 1.128) because MR's T3/T4 estate mass pulls gov up and informal down relative to pure NU.
All realized profiles are single seed-0 generations; no variance estimates (task-permitted, disclosed in results and figure footnote).

Irony worth reporting: the best candidate for a DEVELOPER-first target is Ville Radieuse — the doctrine claiming gov .95 — because 100 uniform T6 tower cells of no-age estate read dev .50-.59 under the priors. The stakeholder-first inversion reproduces D4's flip from the other direction.

Blend fabrics inherit the first-named parent's skeleton, so candidate naming order (canonical paradigm order) materially affects blend geometry and density (NU+MR leaves 86 of NU's 280 build cells vacant because MR's budget is sparser). The order was fixed by convention, not optimized — a 30-candidate ordered search was out of time budget.

Expected profiles for blends use the blended 400-cell budget, but generation reconciles built counts to the fixed skeleton; for NU+MR this under-fill changes token proportions only mildly (reconciliation counts in results_d6.json), and its effect is folded into the reported expectation-vs-realized gap rather than isolated.

choices.choice: Expectation surrogate = per-token pool-average power (GFA-weighted mean of v05 prior vectors over the token pool's LABELED buildings, estates on no_age) times expected labeled GFA per pool cell, normalized by total expected labeled GFA
choices.alternatives: semantic-mix-conditioned expectation (weight pool buildings by the candidate's demanded semantic mix); Monte-Carlo expectation over collage draws
choices.reason: task-specified formula, fully deterministic and generation-free; deliberately ignoring semantic conditioning makes the expectation-vs-realized gap a measurement of what conditioning + collage sampling actually move (it turned out to be the dominant error term: 0.674 L1 for neighbourhood_unit)

choices.choice: Rank by both cosine and L1; on disagreement pick by L1, then post-hoc generate the cosine winner too and report which pick REALIZES closer (added beyond spec)
choices.alternatives: L1 only; cosine only; declare a tie
choices.reason: task rule is L1-decides, but the GOV-first margin (0.0021 expected L1) is far inside surrogate error, so an expectation-level pick alone would be overclaiming; the realized cross-check (0.827 vs 1.128) independently confirmed the blend

choices.choice: Blend generation: first-named parent's skeleton with its civic RESERVED program kept verbatim (T2 carrier, cell-wise semantics looked up from the parent's cached D3 unit); blended built multiset reconciled to available build cells by largest remainder (over-fill) or E_VACANT padding (under-fill, counted); micro-arrangement = 3 Shanghai-accent swap-Gibbs sweeps only
choices.alternatives: blend skeletons cell-wise (geometrically incoherent roads); invent a prescriptive geometry for the blend (would fabricate doctrine the sources never wrote); rescale the skeleton to fit the blend budget
choices.reason: no doctrine prescribes a hybrid's geometry, so asserting one would violate the no-fabrication rule; the Shanghai-accent Gibbs is the project's documented behavior for doctrine-silent arrangement; all reconciliation counts are reported in results_d6.json

choices.choice: Blend per-token semantics = mean of the two parents' per-token demanded-semantic CELL distributions (measured from the cached D3 units), assigned by largest remainder after Gibbs
choices.alternatives: blend the global D2 semantic_mix and distribute independently of token; re-derive semantics from doctrine claims for each blend
choices.reason: preserves the token-semantic coupling each parent doctrine established (e.g., garden-city T7 = industry+arcade, gb50180 T7 = podium retail); global-mix blending would let semantics land on tokens neither parent ever paired them with

choices.choice: Pure-paradigm winners reuse the cached seed-0 D3 units verbatim instead of regenerating
choices.alternatives: regenerate with the same machinery
choices.reason: identical machinery and seed would reproduce the same fabric; reuse guarantees the realized read-back is exactly the D4-audited object (D4 R0 numbers match to 1e-4)

choices.choice: Copied prior_cell/readback verbatim from exp_readback.py with provenance comments instead of importing the module; imported generate_v06 as a module for all generation/render functions
choices.alternatives: import exp_readback (executes the full D4 script at import, rewriting results_d4.json and figures); duplicate generate_v06 logic
choices.reason: exp_readback.py has no main guard, so importing it has side effects on another agent's outputs; generate_v06.py is guard-protected and safe to import, satisfying the no-duplication instruction
